questions.answer: I do, very much. It's my go-to way to unwind at the weekend. I enjoy a good thriller or a thoughtful drama, and I especially like films that are genuinely [[thought-provoking]] long after they've ended.

questions.q: What kind of films are popular in your country?
questions.answer: Commercial action films and romantic dramas have always been popular here, along with Indian and Hollywood blockbusters. Recently, though, some Bangladeshi directors have made [[critically acclaimed]] films that are attracting a younger, more discerning audience.

questions.q: Do you prefer watching films at home or at the cinema?
questions.answer: Both have their charm, but I usually watch at home for the comfort. That said, for a big, visually [[spectacular]] film, the cinema experience is hard to beat, so I save those for the big screen.

questions.q: What was the last film you watched?
questions.answer: It was a historical drama about the Liberation War, which I watched with my father. It was quite heavy in places, but it was [[beautifully shot]], and it sparked a long conversation between us about what my grandparents lived through at that time.

questions.q: Do you think films can help people learn a language?
questions.answer: Without a doubt. My English listening improved a lot through watching films with subtitles. You pick up natural expressions, [[intonation]] and slang that textbooks rarely teach, and it's far more enjoyable than studying grammar.
